title: VPC/On‑Prem Reproducible Benchmark Runner and Regression Guardrails
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Build a reproducible benchmarking harness that can be run by customers (VPC/on-prem) and by Redwood SRE/Perf teams to: measure tokens/sec, p95 latency, peak throughput; detect regressions vs pinned baselines; and generate artifacts (CSV, flamegraphs, dashboards) that can be attached to support/eng review. The runner must be infrastructure-as-code friendly (terraform/ansible), pin model artifact hashes, pin container images and runtime kernels, and capture deterministic workload definitions (seeded RNG, sequence length distribution, KV cache warmup profiles). It should support model variants (fp16, int8/quantized), batch sizes, and dynamic routing fallbacks. The goal is to make customer-reported perf regressions reproducible locally and to provide a standard output format ingestible by Console and our regression detector pipeline.
acceptance_criteria: A reproducible CLI runner and a Terraform/Ansible template that can create the customer-like environment (VPC subnets, node types) with a single command
Workload spec format (YAML) that defines sequence length histogram, prompt templates, concurrency profile, and warmup steps
Outputs: canonical CSV (per-step tokens/sec, p95, p50, throughput), JSON summary, and a folded flamegraph SVG for a single run
Automated regression check: compare run to pinned baseline, flag >10% tokens/sec drop or >20% increase in p95, and produce a human-readable regression report
End-to-end run completes on a small on-prem reference (4x A40 equivalent) within documented time and publishes artifacts to an S3-compatible bucket
Docs + runbook for customers and SREs; example customer workload and a sample reproducible incident analysis included
design_decisions: Use a deterministic workload spec format (YAML) with RNG seed and explicit sequence length histogram to enable byte-for-byte comparable runs
Runner implemented as small Go binary + shell orchestration to avoid Python dependency drift in customer environments
Pin container images with digest; include kernel/driver versions in metadata manifest to track kernel selection impact
Emit both human CSV and canonical line-delimited JSON for downstream ingestion into Console and the regression detector
Integrate optional debug mode that captures perf counters (NVIDIA Nsight/cupti or ROCm counters) and writes folded flamegraphs
Regression detector thresholds are configurable per-customer but default to tokens/sec drop > 10% or p95 increase > 20%
Warmup phase required: run a sequence of cache-filling synthetic requests to establish KV cache steady-state before measurement window

notes: Focus on making runs deterministic for a given workload spec and pinned infra/software stack. Runner must collect enough metadata (model hash, container digest, driver/kernel versions, CPU governor state) to explain variance. Provide clear guidance for customers to reproduce our reference runs in their VPC/on-prem environment.
runbook_short: 1) Checkout bench-runner and download pinned workload YAML
2) Deploy reference infra with provided terraform module
4) Wait for warmup phase to complete, then run measurement window
5) Upload artifacts to S3 bucket and open support ticket with artifact URL
